label: TP
reason: Both alerts represent genuine vulnerabilities. Alert 1 (java/xss): User input from headers flows through URL decode -> doSomething -> bar -> encodeForHTML() -> response.getWriter(). While encodeForHTML exists, it's ONLY in the exception handler (line 87-89), not the normal execution path. On the normal path, bar = param (from user input) goes directly to response.getWriter().println() without encoding. Alert 2 (java/xml/xpath-injection): Same flow - bar (tainted user input) is concatenated into XPath expression at line 72. The switch statement uses guess='ABC' (char 2 = 'C'), so bar=param always. Neither alert has proven mitigation.

evidence.note: User input extracted from headers and URL decoded into param
Switch statement with guess='ABC' always selects case 'C', setting bar=param (no filtering)
XSS sink: bar printed to response.getWriter() without encoding on normal path (encodeForHTML only in catch block)
XPath injection sink: bar concatenated into expression
